newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik aluminium plant sees lower 1996 output.
newsitem.headline: Tajik aluminium plant sees lower 1996 output.

text.p: Tajikistan's Tursunzade aluminium smelter has revised downward its forecast of total 1996 output to over 200,000 tonnes from a targeted 240,000 tonnes, a plant official said on Tuesday.
"In 1996, we will produce more than 200,000 tonnes of primary aluminium," Sadriddin Sharipov, acting chief engineer at the smelter, told Reuters.
He said output this year would definitely not reach 1995's 236,500 tonnes.
Two of the plant's 12 smelting units were shut down in March and Abbas Radzhabov, head of the government's industry department, said Tursunzade was working at only 45 percent of its capacity.

Sharipov said the plant had had problems with supplies of raw materials last month and that some workers had not shown up for work, but denied there had been a total shutdown as reported earlier by the Russian news agency Interfax.
"The factory did not shut down in August, though there were some troubles," he said.
He said Tursunzade's raw materials reserves were low -- at less than a month's supply against an average six-week supply.
Sharipov said electricity supply problems could appear this winter after the neighbouring Central Asian state of Uzbekistan pulled out of an electricity barter arrangement with Tajikistan.
"We expect there will be a deficit of electricity this winter," Sharipov said, but he gave no further details.
Tursunzade, located about 50 km west of the Tajik capital Dushanbe, owes creditors more than $100 million, he said.
Sharipov said plant officials had forwarded a two-stage privatisation plan for the smelter to the Tajik government, which he said was considering the proposal.
Foreign economic relations department head Nikolai Dereshev said the smelter was involved in a $50 million project to reconstruct a unit for enriching anodes.
The plant planned to complete the reconstruction, begun last year, in three or four years, but Dereshev said funding problems could push back the date.
Sharipov also said the plant had invited several foreign firms to Tursunzade to discuss reconstruction of two units but that talks had been inconclusive. --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
